key_insight: DenseNet121 led ten pretrained models in classifying benign versus malignant breast histopathology images, achieving 99.4% test accuracy and 0.999 AUC-ROC.
clinical_relevance: Interpretable image classification could support breast pathology assessment, but these research results do not establish clinical readiness.
method: Benchmarked ten ImageNet-pretrained CNN and transformer models on BreakHis histopathology images.
Used a patient-level split for benign-versus-malignant classification.
Applied Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP; explanations highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions.
evidence_signal: On the BreakHis patient-level test split, DenseNet121 reportedly outperformed all other models (p < 0.001), while transformers trailed CNNs.
watch_item: External validation and prospective clinical evaluation are not reported in the abstract, leaving real-world generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
